description: 2 tactical challenges for Black against the Krejcik Gambit. Counter 2.g4 with 2...d5! or take and hold the pawn.

drills.briefExplanation: 1...f5 2.g4 d5! — play the Dutch and meet the flank push with a central counter.
drills.description: Black to play. White is threatening the Krejcik 2.g4 — play 1...f5 and be ready with 2...d5!.
drills.explanation: The central antidote: after 1...f5 2.g4, Black ignores the wing and plays 2...d5! — striking in the center. White's g4 push now looks silly: the center is Black's, the g-pawn is overextended, and Black will develop with ...Nf6 and ...e6. Meet flank attacks with central breaks — always.
drills.name: The d5 Counter

drills.briefExplanation: 2...fxg4 3.e4 d5! — take the pawn, then strike in the center before White consolidates.
drills.description: Black to play. White played the Krejcik 2.g4 — take and counter with 3...d5!.
drills.explanation: The greedy-and-solid defense: take with 2...fxg4, and after 3.e4 strike 3...d5! — opening the center while White's kingside is loose. After 4.exd5 Qxd5 Black is a pawn up with a centralized queen; White's g4 'sacrifice' only weakened the kingside. Take the material, then play in the center.
drills.name: Take and Break

name: Krejcik Gambit — Black Tactics
